title: Is the simplicity bias real in superposition? Testing whether networks pick the lowest-complexity interpolant on a controlled task

original_idea.body:
# Simplicity Bias in Superposition

Two equally-fitting features (simple vs complex); measure which the network relies on, varying width/depth/weight decay.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain to OOD/goal-misgeneralization but the link to a concrete catastrophic outcome stays broad.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Tiny MLPs on a controlled two-feature task with probes; beginner-accessible.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Independent-friendly: synthetic, one GPU; though simplicity bias is heavily studied.
